guarantees.claim: When key_length_i equals Key_128, i_pad_256 and o_pad_256 are assigned 512-bit values formed by zero-padding secret_key_i[1023:896] to 512 bits and XORing with a constant of repeated 8'h36 (i_pad) or 8'h5c (o_pad); i_pad_512 and o_pad_512 similarly use zero-padding to 1024 bits with the same XOR constants.
When key_length_i equals Key_256, pads are generated with zero-padding of secret_key_i[1023:768] to 512 or 1024 bits and XORing with 8'h36/8'h5c.
When key_length_i equals Key_384, pads use zero-padding of secret_key_i[1023:640] to block sizes and XOR with pad constants.

When key_length_i equals Key_512, i_pad_256 and o_pad_256 are assigned secret_key_i[1023:512] XORed with 8'h36/8'h5c constants directly (no padding needed); i_pad_512 and o_pad_512 zero-pad secret_key_i[1023:512] to 1024 bits then XOR with constants.

When key_length_i equals Key_1024, i_pad_256 and o_pad_256 are forced to all zeros; i_pad_512 and o_pad_512 are assigned secret_key_i[1023:0] XORed with the corresponding 1024-bit pad constants (8'h36/8'h5c).
For any other value of key_length_i (including the default case), all four pad outputs remain at their default value of all zeros.
guarantees.cond: key_length_i not in {Key_128, Key_256, Key_384, Key_512, Key_1024}

assumptions.claim: key_length_i is assumed to take only the defined values (Key_128 through Key_1024) during HMAC key padding; otherwise the pads become zero, which the module does not report as an error.
assumptions.cond: When the HMAC algorithm uses these key pads.
assumptions.risk: Silently using all-zero key pads can allow HMAC computations with a weak or incorrect key, breaking message integrity protection.

assumptions.claim: secret_key_i must be at least 1024 bits wide (bits 1023:0 valid) because the chunk uses bit indices up to 1023.
assumptions.risk: If the actual secret_key_i width is smaller, some bit slices will be out of range or undefined, producing incorrect pad values.

uncertain_points.claim: The unique case default clause leaves all pads at zero when key_length_i is illegal. No error flag is asserted, and the zero pads propagate into the HMAC computation, potentially breaking the MAC security without detection.
uncertain_points.cond: key_length_i takes an invalid value (e.g., due to misconfiguration or fault).
uncertain_points.risk: HMAC results may be produced with an all-zero key pad, effectively weakening or invalidating the authentication tag.

uncertain_points.claim: For a 1024-bit key, the inner and outer pads for SHA-256 are explicitly zeroed because the configuration is 'not allowed'. However, no hardware interlock prevents the HMAC from being operated in SHA-256 mode with this key length; the zero pads are forwarded, and the operation may appear to succeed with a vulnerable key pad.
uncertain_points.cond: System configures HMAC for SHA-256 and selects Key_1024.
uncertain_points.risk: An unsupported combination may be used without raising an error, leading to an HMAC instantiation that does not meet cryptographic requirements.
